title: SonicRoute
tagline: Send each app's audio to the device you choose.
intro: Keep music on your speakers and games or calls on your headset. SonicRoute is a Windows audio utility that lives in the system tray: choose output and input devices for individual apps, control audio with hotkeys, the tray wheel or a panel, and combine routine actions into automation rules.
preview: Interface examples: Quick panel for app volume and devices; automation editor for combining triggers and action steps.

downloadIntro: For most Windows x64 users, the Microsoft Store build offers convenient installation and automatic updates. Choose Lite x64 for a single executable, or Legacy x64 if installing .NET 8 is not convenient. The download link above always points to the latest release; Lite and Legacy links below are for {release}, while the Store page shows the version currently available there.

steps: Start SonicRoute, find its icon in the Windows notification area (it may be under hidden icons), and double-click it to open the full interface.
Select your preferred output and input devices in Settings.
Click the tray icon to open a panel, or set up your hotkeys. Create automation rules when you want to combine actions.
commandNote: `sr` connects only to an already-running SonicRoute instance; it does not start the app. Before first use, start SonicRoute normally to register the command, then close and reopen your terminal. See the {faq} if device switching does not work as expected.

features: **Automatic foreground-app detection.** By default, controls follow the audio app you’re using. With the panel closed, use the same hotkeys to change its volume, mute it, or switch devices, or scroll over the system tray to adjust volume—no need to find the app first.

**Quick panel.** Click the tray icon to manage app volumes in one place. Click an app’s icon to mute it or expand its device section to choose headphones or speakers. Control music players, games, and voice chat apps separately.

**Automation rules.** On the Automation page, arrange device switches, volume changes, and program launches in order, with delays if needed. Save and enable the rule, then run it with a hotkey, when an app starts or gains focus, or on a schedule instead of repeating the steps yourself.
